title: DODB: Distinct Objects, Distinct Boxes
quickIdea: Each distinct object independently picks a box, so k choices per object. Boxes are labelled, so swapping contents between boxes gives a new distribution.
remember: Empty boxes allowed: k^n for n objects into k boxes.
No empty box: k! S(n,k), equivalently the inclusion-exclusion sum.
This is exactly the number of functions from an n-set to a k-set.

example.prompt: 5 distinct balls into 3 distinct boxes, no box empty.

gateAngle: Recognise it as 'functions from a set to a set'. GATE's favourite twist is the onto condition, which converts 3^n into an inclusion-exclusion sum.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many functions from a 4-element set to a 3-element set are onto?
variations.why: 3^4 - 3 x 2^4 + 3 x 1^4 = 81 - 48 + 3 = 36, and 3! S(4,3) = 6 x 6 = 36. The two methods must agree - always check them against each other.

trap.what: Dividing k^n by k! to 'remove box labels'.
trap.why: k^n counts labelled-box distributions. Dividing by k! is only valid when all boxes hold the same number of objects; in general it over-divides.
trap.counterexample: 3 distinct balls into 3 identical boxes: the labelled count is 3^3 = 27, and 27/3! = 4.5 is not even an integer, while the true unlabelled count is S(3,1) + S(3,2) + S(3,3) = 1 + 3 + 1 = 5. Dividing works only in the two-box case by accident.

check.question: How many functions are there from a 4-element set to a 3-element set?
check.explanation: Each of the 4 inputs picks one of 3 outputs: 3^4 = 81.
